text: Zoroastrianism began more than 2,500 years ago in eastern Iran or Central Asia, with the prophet Zarathustra.
Almost nothing is certain about his life, and the Greeks called him Zoroaster.
src: Eastern Iran or Central Asia, in the second or early first millennium BCE (the date is disputed) / others place him in the 7th or 6th century BCE / The prophet Zarathustra (Zoroaster)
Almost nothing is certain about his life / the prophet Zarathustra, known to the Greeks as Zoroaster

text: Zoroastrians believe that Ahura Mazda, the Wise Lord, is the good creator of all that is good.
Every person is called to choose truth over the lie, with “good thoughts, good words, good deeds”.
src: Zoroastrianism teaches that Ahura Mazda is the wise and good creator of all that is good / Ahura Mazda, the “Wise Lord”
calls every person to choose truth over the lie / The ethical motto of the faith is “good thoughts, good words, good deeds”

text: Fire is a sign of Ahura Mazda’s light, though Zoroastrians do not see fire itself as a god.
Fire temples keep sacred fires burning all the time, some of them for centuries.
src: fire, the symbol of Ahura Mazda’s light and truth / they do not regard fire itself as a god
Fire temples keep sacred fires burning continuously, the most important of which have burned for centuries

text: It was the faith of Persian kings, and the Sasanian Empire of Ardashir I made it the state religion.
After the Arab conquest of Iran, it slowly became the faith of a small number of people.
src: It was the faith of the Achaemenid kings and the state religion of the Parthian and Sasanian empires / Ardashir I founds the Sasanian Empire, under which Zoroastrianism becomes the state religion
After the Arab conquest of Iran it became a minority faith / Conversion to Islam was gradual

text: Heavy taxes and persecution left small communities around the desert cities of Yazd and Kerman.
Some Zoroastrians sailed to India, and their descendants became known as the Parsis, “Persians”.
src: heavy taxation, social pressure and periods of persecution reduced them to small communities, concentrated around the desert cities of Yazd and Kerman
a group sailed to Gujarat / Their descendants became known as the Parsis, “Persians”

text: In 1892 the Parsi Dadabhai Naoroji became the first Asian elected to the British Parliament.
Today perhaps 100,000 to 200,000 Zoroastrians live mainly in India, Iran and around the world.
src: 1892: The Parsi Dadabhai Naoroji becomes the first Asian elected to the British House of Commons
Perhaps 100,000 to 200,000, mainly in India (the Parsis), Iran and the diaspora
